---

### 1. 🦪 Lucania — Ferry Building, Embarcadero
**📍 1 Ferry Building | Opening: Early October 2026 | 💰 $$–$$$**


The Ferry Building's most prominent vacant space is finally reopening with Lucania, from the team behind A16, the Italian standby on Chestnut Street in the Marina. While A16 specializes in Neapolitan pizza, Lucania will focus on southern Italy.
 
The name means "land of light," and restaurateur Shelley Lindgren has said, "Lucania brings together nearly three decades of experience in San Francisco's food and wine world, inspired by the traditions of Southern Italy."
 
Lucania will bring the 140-seat, dog-friendly patio just off Embarcadero Plaza — formerly occupied by MarketBar Cafe, which closed in April 2020 — back to life.


---

### 2. 🥩 Monami — Pacific Heights
**📍 2001 Fillmore St. | Opening: Fall 2026 | 💰 $$$$**


The next restaurant from the owners of Michelin-starred Korean restaurant Ssal in San Francisco is a modern steakhouse dedicated to premium beef. Owners Junsoo and Hyunyoung Bae will open Monami this fall at 2001 Fillmore St. in Pacific Heights.
 
Junsoo Bae told the Chronicle that Monami will steer away from the all-you-can-eat format often seen at Korean barbecue restaurants — it will serve both an à la carte and tasting menu — and focus on premium cuts of Californian, Japanese and Korean beef.
 
A follow-up to Best Award of Excellence winner Ssal, Monami draws from chef Junsoo's tenure at Meadowood and Hyunyoung's experience at Grand Award winner the French Laundry.


---

### 3. 🇮🇹 Sutro Hall — SoMa
**📍 140 New Montgomery St. | Opening: November 2026 (previewing fall) | 💰 $$$$**


Sutro Hall will fill a ground-floor restaurant space at 140 New Montgomery that has sat empty for almost two years, ever since the upscale Moroccan restaurant Mourad closed in October 2024. Now Doug Washington and a team of industry veterans plan to open Sutro Hall, a California-Mediterranean restaurant, in November.
 
Executive chef Michael Magallanes' menu will focus on grilled meats and vegetables, such as skewered short ribs with date jus and melted leeks, and roasted carrots with lentils.


---

### 4. 🍣 Shinka — Financial District
**📍 334 Battery St. (inside The Jay Hotel) | Opening: October 2026 | 💰 $$$$**


The ground-floor space inside The Jay in FiDi is set to become Shinka, marrying Japanese sensibilities and French techniques. It's the first Bay Area restaurant by executive chef and Jean-Georges alum Fumio Yonezawa.
 
It will open with a tasting menu; à la carte options will follow.

### 5. 🥗 Olive Juice — Lower Haight
**📍 354 Divisadero St. | Opened: October 8, 2026 | 💰 $–$$**


Hannah Collins Tate, a hospitality and branding pro, is turning a former Kelly-Moore Paints store into Olive Juice, a cafe that aspires to transcend the moralizing clichés of wellness culture. It debuted for outdoor dining on the back patio, with indoor dining beginning early next year. ### 7. 🏃 Run Club SF — Weekly Runs
**📍 Golden Gate Park / Kezar Stadium | 📅 Tues, Wed & Thurs nights + Sat mornings | 💰 Free**


Run Club SF meets Tuesday nights in Golden Gate Park for wildcard runs, Wednesday nights at Kezar Stadium for Runner Strength Workouts, and Thursday nights at Kezar Stadium for speedwork — always hosting a casual post-run social on Tuesday and Thursday nights.
 
They also meet on Saturday mornings for adventure runs all over the city that often include a casual post-run brunch.
